reason: Adding ligaments is the only offered combination and should support the elbow.

effect: The ligaments complete the movable arm skeleton, stabilizing the elbow against sideways movement while allowing bending.
reaction: The arrows make the distinction between movement and support clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building living bone was most worthwhile: the planned cutaways connect embedded cells and their tiny channels to nutrient supply, making hard bone feel like living tissue.

leastWorthwhile.text: The joint assembly became predictable because each addition was the only offered combination, although the planned illustrations explained its function.

surprise.text: The lineage picture changed my understanding by showing that some matrix-producing osteoblasts become embedded osteocytes connected through small channels.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, but terms such as osteoblast and osteocyte were introduced without explicit definitions; their roles had to be inferred from the picture description.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the movable skeleton is connected to muscles, though I would hope for more meaningful choices than the largely single-option sequence here.
